processing: Little is documented for this cultivar alone. As with other Japanese black teas, leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, usually in small batches.
harvest_season: Not well recorded for this cultivar. Japanese black teas are commonly picked in spring and summer.
appearance_dry: Typical of Japanese black tea, dark twisted leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Japanese black tea, a clear reddish amber.
appearance_wet: Typical of Japanese black tea, soft coppery brown leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description exists for this cultivar on its own; Japanese black teas tend toward a gentle, lightly sweet cup with little harshness.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Japanese black tea. Taste at the short end, since these teas are usually better without force.

vintage_note: As is usual for Japanese black tea, it is sold in small lots by the current or last harvest year, often with grower and cultivar named on the packet. Drink within a year or two for the freshest aroma.
description:
Benifuji is a Japanese tea cultivar listed for black tea. Its name begins with beni, the Japanese word for crimson that also appears in several other black tea cultivar names. Little else is documented about it.

As with other Japanese black teas, it would be made by withering, rolling, oxidising and drying, most often by small growers.

The usual cup from this class is soft and gently sweet, so brew it a little under the boil and avoid long steeps. If you find a lot, the grower's own description is your best guide to this cultivar.
history: Little is documented about where and when Benifuji was bred, who released it, or how widely it is planted today.
